newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR LIFTS INDIA WITH UNBEATEN 117.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR LIFTS INDIA WITH UNBEATEN 117.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar stroked an unbeaten 117 to rescue India from a shaky start against Sri Lanka on the second day of the second and final test on Sunday.
Captain Tendulkar's 13th test century, and second in successive matches, took India from nine for two to 226 for four at the close in reply to Sri Lanka's first innings of 332.

Tendulkar made the most of his one escape, on 34, when his opposite number Arjuna Ranatunga dived to his left at first slip but failed to hold onto a sharp chance off pace bowler Ravindra Pushpakumara.
Ranatunga did not take to the field for the rest of the day, nursing a sore left thumb.
Tendulkar brought up his second successive century by flicking Pushpakumara off his legs for his 13th four in 241 minutes and 154 balls. He scored 143 in the drawn first test.
The Indian skipper found his most effective ally in Saurav Ganguly, who hit an unbeaten 47.

Left-hander Ganguly came in when Mohammad Azharuddin was out for 22 in the second over after tea to make the score 126 for four, and shared an unfinished fifth wicket stand of exactly 100 with Tendulkar.
India had initially been jolted when Chaminda Vaas struck an early blow by having Ajay Jadeja edge a catch to wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana for one when the total was two.
Sajeeva de Silva, the other left-arm seamer in the side, sent back Rahul Dravid for two when the batmsan hooked a short delivery down to Vaas at long leg.
Sri Lanka, 316 for seven overnight, were all out for 332, losing their last three wickets in 38 minutes.
Debutant fast-medium bowler Debasis Mohanty took four for 78, including Sri Lanka's top scorer Aravinda de Silva, who added only two to his overnight 144.
De Silva batted for 365 minutes, faced 228 balls and hit 20 fours in compiling his 13th test century.
Muthiah Muralitharan, who figured in a 48-run stand for the eighth wicket with de Silva, fell to leg-spinner Anil Kumble for 39, his highest test score.
